alternate_names: Sri Balaji and Sri Kartikeya Temple
deities: Lord Balaji (Sri Venkateswara; presiding deity; 6-feet tall idol in the lower sanctum sanctorum)
Lord Kartikeya (Muruga, with consorts Valli and Deivanai; 3-feet tall idol in the upper sanctum sanctorum)

history.dynasty: None documented; administered by the Motibagh Shri Skanda Samaj (Balaji and Kartikeya Temple Trust)
history.period: Modern (verify - no documented establishment date found in sources)
history.summary: The Sri Balaji and Sri Kartikeya Temple sits atop the scenic Seminary Hills, about 6 km north-west of Nagpur, and is one of the city's most revered Hindu shrines, serving Nagpur's large South Indian community. It enshrines Lord Balaji (a manifestation of Lord Vishnu) in the lower sanctum with a 6-feet tall idol, and Lord Kartikeya (Muruga), the mythological commander of the gods' army, with consorts Valli and Deivanai in the upper sanctum with a 3-feet tall idol. The temple is noted for its architectural beauty: a three-tier structure with Ekadala Vimana and a 60-feet high Rajagopuram, blending South Indian (Rajagopuram) and North Indian (mandapam) orders. The complex includes a well-maintained flower garden and Tulsi garden at the entrance, a community hall, a library, residential quarters for priests, and a Vedic Pathshala for training in the Hindu Vedic Shastras. The trust is run by the Motibagh Shri Skanda Samaj, and the temple doubles as a cultural centre hosting artistic, cultural and spiritual activities. No documented founding date was found in any source (verify).

name: Balaji Temple Seminary Hills
town_description: Nagpur is a major city of Maharashtra and its second capital, one of the leading commercial centres of the state. It is a major rail junction, well connected to all four metropolitan cities of India, and served by the Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport. The city has a sizeable South Indian population and many South Indian temples, of which the Balaji Temple atop the scenic Seminary Hills, about 6 km north-west of the city centre, is among the most revered.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur (nearest airport, well connected to Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai and Kolkata; taxis and app cabs available). Distance from Seminary Hills approx. 12-15 km (verify).
travel.railway: Nagpur Railway Station (Nagpur Junction), one of the leading rail junctions of India, well connected to all four metros and major cities; approx. 6 km south-east of the temple (verify).
travel.road: About 6 km north-west of Nagpur city centre atop Seminary Hills. City buses, taxis and auto-rickshaws readily available; buses are cheap and cover most of the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Brahmotsavam and Skanda Shashti are the grandest times to visit but draw heavy crowds; weekday mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 11:00 AM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify - one listing shows mornings from 7:00 AM). No entry fee; donations welcome. Modest dress expected; photography generally restricted inside the main shrine.
